quote: 1. Traders have to take their ego and throw it in a trash can when walking into the trading day because they are going to be wrong.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 2. If you want to reap big gains in the market, make up your mind right now that you are going to separate trading from your ego. It's more important to make money than it is to be right.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 3. Soros has taught me that when you have tremendous conviction on a trade, you have to go for the jugular. It takes courage to be a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 4. Bad news is sometimes the best buying opportunity life gives you.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 5. Amateurs think about how much money they can make. Professionals think about how much money they could lose.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 6. Trade what you see, not what you think.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 7. If you're extremely confident, taking a loss doesn't bother you.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 8. When I've looked at all the investors that have very large reputations — Warren Buffett, Carl Icahn, George Soros — they all only have one thing in common. It is to make large concentrated bets where they have a lot of conviction.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 9. Stocks should be at a profit the first day you buy them.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 10. Not losing big is the single most important factor for winning big. As a speculator, losing is not a choice, but how much you lose is.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 11. Soros is the best loss taker I've ever seen. He doesn't care whether he wins or loses on a trade. If a trade doesn't work, he's confident enough about his ability to win on other trades that he can easily walk away from the position.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 12. Looking at the biggest winners, we found that in many cases, the earnings had been on the table for a while.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 13. The first thing I heard when I got in the business - not from my mentor - was, 'Bulls make money, bears make money, and pigs get slaughtered.' I'm here to tell you I was a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 14. You must adjust your risk as a function of potential reward.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 15. I try not to get too complicated. I look at the daily Dow and that works but it's not foolproof.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 16. Look at your own life. You can get so many stock ideas from just what you're buying. … From examining your own life, you can come up with unbelievable, great investing ideas.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 17. The way to build superior long-term returns is through preservation of capital and home runs.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 18. There's no reason you should always be long. If you're sure a bear market is coming — go to cash.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 19. Success in investing doesn't correlate with I.Q. once you're above the level of 125. Once you have ordinary intelligence, what you need is the temperament to control the urges that get other people into trouble in investing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 20. In investing, when I hear the word 'conviction' I run like a deer. All the biggest financial collapses in history were caused by smart people with conviction. I would bet on a person with average intelligence that respects risk over a genius with conviction any day of the week.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 21. The cup-and-handle is one of the better ones but it does not show up nearly as often as people might think. A cup-and-handle really has to occur in a general market correction.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 22. My favorite quote of all time is maybe Mark Twain: 'Put all your eggs in one basket and watch the basket carefully.' I tend to think that's what great investors do.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 23. To have lasting success in the stock market, you must decide once and for all that it's more important to make money than to be right. Your ego must take a backseat.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 24. Learn to buy weakness and sell strength, and not buy strength and sell weakness; because you're just going to continue to get whipsawed.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 25. Calculating risks shrewdly is the main ingredient for consistent superior performance. Pros play percentage ball, and that's why, in the long run, they are more consistent than amateurs.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 26. Too many investors look at the present. The present is already in the price. You have to think out of the box and visualize 18-24 months from now, what the world is going to be and what securities might trade at.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 27. I look for support points that have held in the past or previous highs the stock has pulled back down on to.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 28. The wonderful thing about our business is that it's liquid, and you can wipe the slate clean on any day.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 29. The single most important advice I can give anybody is: Learn from your mistakes. That is the only way to become a successful trader.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 30. Virtually every superperformance phase in big, winning stocks occurred while the stock price was in a definite price uptrend. In almost every case, the trend was identifiable early in the superperformance advance.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 31. I think diversification and all the stuff they're teaching at business school today is probably the most misguided concept everywhere.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 32. If you're early on in your career and they give you a choice between a great mentor or higher pay, take the mentor every time. It's not even close.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 33. Your stop loss should be a calculation as a function of expected gain. Then you back into risk based on your own personal math. That's the holy grail; managing the risk/reward relationship.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 34. Trading without a stop-loss is like driving a car without brakes. Those who trade without stops, eventually stop trading.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 35. I think investment psychology is by far the most important element, followed by risk control, with the least important consideration being the question of where you buy and sell.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 36. One of my favorite patterns is the tendency for the markets to move from relative lows to relative highs and vice versa every two to four days... It takes several days of a market rallying before it looks really good. That's when everyone wants to buy it, and that's the time when the professionals, like myself, are selling. Conversely, when the market has been down for a few days, and everyone is bearish, that's the time I like to be buying.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 37. To compound your money, and not your mistakes, your goal is to buy on the way up—not on the way down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 38. If you don't feel like a fool, you're not managing risk.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 39. You must have a love for the market in order to be successful in this game.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 40. Do not invest in the present. The present is not what moves stock prices.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 41. Long-term success in the stock market has nothing to do with hope or luck. Winning stock traders have rules and a well-thought-out plan. Conversely, losers lack rules, or if they have rules, they don't stick to them for very long; they deviate.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 42. I cut the losers very quickly. The maximum loss I allow is 7%.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 43. My results went from average to stellar when I finally made the choice that I was going to make every trade an intelligent risk/reward decision.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 44. It was all because I got emotional and dropped every tool of discipline I've ever had.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 45. When you tell yourself, I'm going to break my rule just this one time, you open the door to losing discipline, because it's never just 'one time.'
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 46. I've always loved to play games, and face it: investing is one big game. You need to be decisive, open-minded, flexible and competitive.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 47. Chart patterns are not the cause; they're the effect. Human behavior hasn't changed and isn't likely to change much in the future.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 48. You can tell a lot by volume. If the volume doubles one day and the stock moves to a new high, it is telling you a lot of people are interested in the stock and buying it.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 49. I believe that good investors are successful not because of their IQ, but because they have an investing discipline. But, what is more disciplined than a machine? A well-researched machine can make many average investors redundant, leaving behind only the really good human investors with exceptional intuition and skill.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 50. The best risk control is knowing what you are doing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 51. You don't have to involve yourself in every market movement. In fact, you should not attempt to. Be an exacting opportunist. Be selective and pick your entry spots very carefully. Wait until the probabilities are stacked in your favor before you act.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 52. The first thing I do is figure out how much money I could lose.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 53. I like putting all my eggs in one basket and then watching the basket very carefully.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 54. If you want to be the best, you have to do things that other people are unwilling to do.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 55. There really is no intelligent reason to increase your trading size if your positions are showing losses.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 56. I study the market because I want to do it and because I'm fascinated to find out what makes the stock go up and what is going to be the next big winning stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 57. Concentrating your bets decreases your overall risk because where you tend to be in trouble is if you have 35 or 40 names. If you have a big massive position, it has your attention.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 58. Do your homework. Recap the day. What do I want to happen tomorrow? What happens if the opposite occurs? What happens if nothing happens? Think through all the 'what-ifs.' Anticipate and plan, rather than react.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 59. Soros's great gift was how to use leverage, and how much money to have down based on the risk/reward and your sense of conviction.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 60. The more disciplined you can get, the better you are going to do in the market.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 61. I put a lot more weight into how this stock is acting relative to the S&P — you can see real divergences when stocks are making new highs and the relative strength line is not.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 62. Practice does not make perfect. Only perfect practice makes perfect.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 63. With every trade I make, my approach is always 'risk-first.' By thinking and acting 'risk-first,' you know exactly what you stand to lose if you're wrong, which in trading is far more important than what you stand to gain if you're right, because if you lose all your chips, the game is over.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 64. You want some institutional ownership, because they really power a stock higher, but you don't want too much sponsorship. I would say 1% to 20% is the ideal range.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 65. My goal is not to buy at the lowest or cheapest price but at the 'right' price, just as a stock is ready to move significantly higher. Trying to pick a bottom is unnecessary and a waste of time; it misses the whole point.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 66. I've also never hung onto a security if the reason I bought it has changed. That's when you need to sell.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 67. Therefore, you want to cut your losses quickly.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 68. It takes courage to ride a profit with huge leverage.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 69. Once the relative strength starts falling off, I usually get out of the stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 70. Governments defending prices against fundamentals always lose.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 71. You can make money or you can make excuses. But you can't make both.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 72. If you try to learn from every single trade that you make, you are only going to get better and better as time goes on.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 73. Once you make a lot of money, it's incredibly enjoyable to give it away. It's a way to satisfy the soul.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 74. Being wrong is acceptable, but staying wrong is totally unacceptable.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 75. I went from mediocre to a stellar performer when I told myself: To heck with worrying about the money and obsessing over the scoreboard. I'm just going to focus on being the best trader I can be and sticking to the rules.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 76. I'm always thinking about losing money as opposed to making money. Don't focus on making money; focus on protecting what you have.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 77. You may feel dumb breaking even on a trade that was once at a profit; however, you'll feel a lot worse if you turn a good-size gain into a loser.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 78. The idea of studying the greatest stocks of all time to see what made them great made a lot of sense to me.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 79. I never try to make money in the stock market. I buy on the assumption that they could close the market the next day and not reopen it for five years.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 80. The mistake I'd say 98% of money managers and individuals make is they feel like they got to be playing in a bunch of stuff. And if you really see it, put all your eggs in one basket and then watch that basket very carefully.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 81. I look at the five-year earnings growth record and the last two quarters of earnings relative to the previous year's levels.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 82. One of the most important things to do is to not play when you don't see a fat pitch.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 83. Everyone has a stop loss. For some, it's when they go broke. Then they take the ultimate stop loss... they quit trading!
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 84. Every time I buy a stock, I write down the reasons why I bought it. Doing this helps cement in my mind the characteristics of a winning stock. Maybe even more important, it helps me learn from my mistakes.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 85. I never use valuation to time the market. I use liquidity considerations and technical analysis for timing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 86. What I learned was sizing is 70 or 80% of the equation. It's not whether you're right or wrong. It's about how much you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 87. You're the manager, and it's up to you to protect your hard-earned capital.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 88. It's amazing how well you can do if you start compounding your money. If you start getting some very nice returns each year, that small amount of money can really build itself into a very substantial amount.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 89. Growth comes from having the courage to look at the difficult times and dissect what went wrong.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 90. The relative strength is very important. Again, I look for at least above 80, and preferably above 90.
speaker: David Ryan
